ambiguities.issue: The precise quantifier intended by 'with high probability (say, 0.9)' is not formalized.
ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p.11; printed p.22, Exercise 2.4.3] The source combines the asymptotic phrase 'with high probability' with the parenthetical fixed level 'say, 0.9'.
ambiguities.impact: A probability tending to 1 is stronger than an eventual probability of at least 0.9. The contract therefore preserves both the source phrase and its explicit 0.9 benchmark rather than silently choosing one as the sole meaning.

ambiguities.evidence: [PDF p.11; printed p.22, Exercise 2.4.3] Both the hypothesis d = O(1) and conclusion O(log n / log log n) use big-O notation without naming constants or their dependencies.
ambiguities.impact: A restatement must not assume without justification either one universal degree constant for all bounded-degree families or unrestricted dependence on the chosen family; any explicit constant-dependence convention should be identified.

ambiguities.impact: The base changes the quotient only by asymptotically harmless constant-level effects, and sufficiently large n avoids the finite-domain issue; a formal finite-n theorem may nevertheless need to choose these conventions explicitly.

contract_plain_english: [PDF p.10, printed p.21, Section 2.4 definitions; PDF p.11, printed p.22, standing paragraph and Exercise 2.4.3] Let n grow and allow p to vary with n. Form the Erdos-Renyi graph G(n,p), where distinct vertex pairs are connected independently with probability p, and write d = (n - 1)p for the common expected degree. If d stays bounded, then, with high probability (the source offers success probability 0.9 as a concrete target), every vertex simultaneously has degree at most a constant times log n / log log n for all sufficiently large n. The source leaves the exact high-probability quantifier and hidden-constant dependencies implicit.
